source.title: Modulating Regularization Frequency for Efficient Compression-Aware Model Training
source.authors: Dongsoo Lee; Se Jung Kwon; Byeongwook Kim; J. Yun; Baeseong Park; Yongkweon Jeon

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and supplementary material; no material truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own results that qualify how an explicit regularization intervention affects held-out accuracy, including cases where accuracy is insensitive to regularization frequency or worse at high frequency. It does not test the claim's central memorization/generalization coexistence proposition.
record.gate_note: Results about compression and regularization frequency bear on V6 only where they directly report test accuracy or perplexity under dropout or weight decay. The cited dropout findings are prior work and are not rows. Weight decay results are not dropout results. No results test random-label memorization, optimizer comparisons, large-batch generalization, sharpness measures from V7, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: Appendix Figure 14 reports the study's own batch-size versus held-out accuracy results and their dependence on weight decay, bearing on V5. The fixed-epoch requirement is not documented for this experiment. Weight decay and compression experiments do not test V6's dropout claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that regularization frequency controls effective regularization strength and that an empirically selected non-regularization period can improve compression-aware accuracy compared with compression every mini-batch.
record.recipe_differences: The study changes the frequency of weight decay, noise insertion, and model compression; it does not test the versions' interventions or outcomes directly. Weight decay is decoupled from the loss in the described experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports accuracy or perplexity varying with non-regularization period and regularization strength; for compression, results also depend on compression type and ratio. It states that pruning accuracy fluctuates negligibly across many periods but drops at pNR=500.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing weight-decay or weight-noise frequency changes accuracy and perplexity; occasional compression can outperform compression every mini-batch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularization frequency and intervention strength jointly affect held-out performance during compression-aware training.

fits_no_version.finding: Tucker-decomposition-induced training-loss changes diminish during training, interpreted as finding compression-tolerant minima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Occasional decomposition can train networks to tolerate the particular compression transformation.

record.problems: No direct results for the listed claim versions. Several compression comparisons measure accuracy after compression rather than a training-test gap. Some results are shown only in figures; supplementary tables are flattened in the supplied text. The authors note that pNR is empirically searched.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows for V6: the study did not evaluate dropout, and the reported weight-decay and compression results do not measure dropout's effect. All cited dropout results are prior work and excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons and optimizer-specific remedies.
A confirmed fixed-epoch batch-size comparison; longer training, warmup, normalization changes, and language-model batch-size effects.
Dropout addition, strength, training-set-size dependence, and joint removal with weight decay under augmentation. Section 6.1 excludes dropout but supplies no dropout ablation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by label memorization versus random removal.

missing.what: Batch-size × weight-decay accuracy results at pNR=1, including the fixed-factor penalty and its recovery with stronger decay. These are not declared in rows_left_out.

Whether Figure 14 holds epochs, updates, or another training budget fixed, and whether learning-rate schedules change with batch size. The supplied text does not specify this sufficiently to establish V5's fixed-epoch condition.
missing.locator: Appendix B, Figure 14 and accompanying caption

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly overlooks Figure 14 when declaring no batch-size results. Its V6 tested_not_extracted designation should instead be not_tested. Compression comparisons, cited variational-dropout results, and the unsupported assertion that excluding dropout improves LeNet accuracy do not establish a dropout effect.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label generalization.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification performance.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Large versus small batch held-out performance under epoch budgets.
Dropout itself is not added or evaluated. The paper tests weight decay, noise insertion, pruning, quantization, and low-rank compression instead.
No magnitude-aware perturbation measure or comparison of generalization-gap predictors.
No influence-based removal of memorized examples.

relationships.condition: ResNet-32 on CIFAR-10, fixed weight decay factor 0.0005 and pNR=1; training budget unspecified.
relationships.reason: Figure 14, missing from the rows, reports accuracy falling from 93.0% at batch 32 to 89.9% at batch 1024; this supports the batch-size penalty component, without establishing fixed-epoch behavior.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy was lower with larger batches at fixed weight decay, but the comparison remains unverified and epoch budgets are unspecified.
